main_text.head: SACRA MEDICINA, MANVS DEORVM.
ΣΥΝΟ'ΨΙΟΣ EIVSDEM
main_text.p: ANIMVM ita quidem PHILOSOPHIA expo-lit: eius tamen expolitionis vix ullus constare fructus poteft; nisi quòd optandū ille putabat, CORPORE quoq; fruatur sano. Iuuenalis in Satyr. Corpus absq; Anima infeliciter curari. Plato in Timaeo.

Eheu dolendum sane est, quod fere communi omnium Excellentium Virorum calamitate ita comparatum, videamus; ut qui in optimarum artium studijs enituntur αἰὲν ἀριστεύειν [?]ἠδὲ ὑπέροχον ἔμμεναι ἄλλων, semper minus caeteris corpore valere, pluribusq; aegritudinum generib. defungi comperiantur. Homerus Iliad. ζ. & λ. Marsil. Ficin. de studiof. san. tuenda, Li. c. 1.
Quanquam non ita dolendum esse censeo, ubi Sanitatis iactura, longè nobiliori Intellectus & Animi valetudine & bono compensatur.
Qua de re, antequam instituti huius operis ὑποθε-[?]σιν[?] proponam, illud praefari cupio.

Si Animi nostri absq; Corporis huiusce auxilio, omnia sua intelligendo, atq; agendo obire possent; utiq; Sanitas omninò contemnenda esset, quò Animo magis proprijs laboribus vacare liceret. Cl. H. Mer-

page.notes: Lower-case "f" in "s" forms throughout is long s, rendered as s. The Greek in paragraph II ("αἰὲν ἀριστεύειν … ἄλλων") is a Homer quotation whose exact letters are not fully legible at this scan resolution; the ἠδὲ and the Greek of paragraph IV (line-broken "ὑποθε-/σιν") are uncertain and marked [?]. The Greek heading "ΣΥΝΟ'ΨΙΟΣ" is copied as printed. The word "Mer-" at the end of the last paragraph continues in the catchword "curial." (Mercurial). No page number is printed separately; "D 2" is the gathering signature. No running head is printed on this page.
